requirements.requirement: Reclaim storage by hardlinking identical release-cache payloads only when ownership and mode match.
requirements.summary: The two 0644 root-owned payload copies initially had distinct inodes. The real pass linked exactly one file, saved 1.81 KiB, and the pair subsequently shared inode 262330 with link count 2. The identical 0600 file remained separate.

requirements.requirement: Preserve every pathname, byte, ownership, and mode; keep differently permissioned files independent and mutable files independently writable.
requirements.summary: All five prepared file paths remained present with matching SHA-256 digests, ownership, modes, and sizes. private.dat remained 0600 on its own inode; mutable/active.dat remained writable at 0644 with link count 1 and an inode distinct from the linked payloads. These properties also survived restart.

requirements.requirement: Ensure a later cache deduplication pass makes no further changes.
requirements.summary: Dry-run passes both before and after restart reported zero linked files and zero bytes saved.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic were unchanged from the prepared state through final collection. The already-installed util-linux hardlink 2.39.3 executed successfully on that platform; no package or OS change was made.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Eligible duplicate payloads were deduplicated without altering content, paths, ownership, or permissions; protected and mutable files stayed independent; repeat passes were idempotent; and the OS/kernel remained unchanged. The mandatory restart protocol is complete and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities and recovered-state checks.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The hardlink operation was the required storage change (cmd-b4a9aec694874c7c). The transient scheduled reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol (cmd-6fa71df013ad41c0); direct post-restart observations showed a new boot identity, healthy system, recovered data, no failed services, unchanged package health, and no persistent unexpected exposure or residue. The changed temporary-service directories and process identifiers are normal consequences of reboot.
